reason: The intestinal collecting veins and portal branches have matching ends and together can form the route from the gut to the liver.
expectation: They will form a portal vessel carrying nutrient-rich intestinal blood toward the liver.

effect: The portal vessel now links the intestinal and liver capillary beds, and it fits the digestive tube's remaining slot.
reaction: The two-bed route makes the liver's position before general circulation clear.
reason: The digestive tube has a named empty slot for the newly created portal vessel.
expectation: The portal vessel will connect the intestine to the liver in the digestive model.

effect: The portal vessel is installed in the digestive tube; the liver's exit route still needs connecting.
reason: The liver collecting veins carry blood out of the liver, and the vena cava junction has openings for them.
expectation: The hepatic veins will connect the liver's blood outflow to the vena cava.

effect: The liver's outflow now connects to the vena cava and right atrium; the digestive model and body circulation still need joining.
reaction: The separate entry and exit routes make the blood flow easier to follow.
reason: The completed digestive tube and hepatic venous return are the two visible parts of the liver's circulation.
expectation: The liver's portal entry and venous exit will be joined in the digestive model.

alternatives.reason: The digestive organs also need to connect to the wider body circulation.

effect: The attempted pairing instead automatically connected the digestive tube to the body; the hepatic venous exit remains to be attached.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the intended order, though my initial pairing was wrong.
reason: The body's liver exit is highlighted as the remaining connection, and hepatic venous return leads to the vena cava.
expectation: The hepatic veins will complete the liver's return route to the body's circulation.

effect: The hepatic venous return completes the digestive connection to the body's circulation; absorbed nutrients still need to be followed through the liver.
reaction: The highlighted route makes the two liver inputs and venous exit clear, though “sinusoids” is not explained.
reason: The remaining nutrient item belongs on the newly connected portal route.
expectation: The model will follow absorbed glucose and amino acids through the liver and onward.

effect: The nutrient view completes the route: some glucose and amino acids move toward liver cells, while others leave in blood. It also identifies sinusoids as broad capillary channels.
reaction: Seeing the nutrients split between liver cells and outgoing blood made the route more meaningful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the portal vessel was most worthwhile: its planned illustration labels both capillary beds and explains why the liver encounters absorbed substances before the wider circulation.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to attach hepatic venous return directly to the digestive tube was the least useful passage, although compatibility feedback automatically advanced the assembly.

surprise.text: The liver receives a separate arterial supply as well as portal blood; the illustration also keeps bile ducts distinct from the blood vessels.

arbitrary.text: The required assembly order was not obvious: the digestive tube had to join the body before the already constructed hepatic venous return could be attached.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see more connections between systems; the nutrient route made the anatomical construction useful for following a physiological process.
